review_outputs.codex-adv:
FINDING 1: A healthy, caught-up PostgreSQL standby is reported as unknown and triggers the replay-lag alert during normal idle periods.
FILE: docs/prism-postgres-exporter-queries.yaml:9
SCENARIO: `pg_stat_replication` contains `prism_standby_1`, but PostgreSQL sets `replay_lag=NULL` after the caught-up standby has been idle → SQL converts it to `-1`; `docs/prism-postgres-alert-rules.json:6` treats `< 0` as failure and fires `PrismHAStandbyReplayLagHigh` after one minute despite `count=1` and `pg_up=1`.
SEVERITY: major

FINDING 2: The connected-client migration changes the threshold from a network-wide total to a per-instance minimum.
FILE: docs/prism-native-alert-rules.json:55
SCENARIO: Two fresh `qbit-prism` instances report six connections each → the deployed expression removed at `docs/prism-alert-rules-qbit-tools.patch:212` sums to 12 and remains healthy, while the replacement at patch line 224 evaluates `6 < 10` independently for both instances and emits two alerts after three minutes. All committed scenarios use a single instance, so this regression passes.
SEVERITY: major
review_outputs.codex-adv-corrections:
FINDING 1: Gate-independent deletion generation leaves disabled, previously provisioned alerts active in Grafana.
FILE: scripts/generate_prism_alerts.py:113
SCENARIO: Grafana already contains `qbit-prism-connected-clients`; render with `qbit_monitoring_stack_prism_alert_connected_clients_enabled=false` → line 141 removes the rule from `groups`, but its UID remains in `kept_uids`, so no `deleteRules` entry is emitted and Grafana retains the active legacy alert. The deployment test still passes because line 91 compares against the same gate-independent UID set.
SEVERITY: major

FINDING 2: D3 reports a synchronous standby as healthy despite requiring an asynchronous topology.
FILE: docs/prism-postgres-exporter-queries.yaml:13
SCENARIO: Set `synchronous_standby_names='FIRST 1 (prism_standby_1)'` while the single standby is streaming and caught up → `count=1`, `known=true`, positions match, and both D3 alerts return healthy because `sync_state` is never queried. PRISM acknowledgements now wait for that standby and can stall when it disappears, contradicting the required asynchronous money-path behavior without any alert.
SEVERITY: major
